summary: Masaya and Career Soft's large-scale tactical RPG series, covering the Genesis/Saturn mainline games, remakes, Japan-only spin-offs, 3DS revival, and mobile entry.

entries.title: Langrisser (Warsong)
entries.definitive_edition: Langrisser I & II remake on Windows

emulation.notes: No emulation needed for the primary route; emulate Genesis, PC Engine, Saturn, or PlayStation only for version comparison.

primary.why: The 2019/2020 Langrisser I & II remake is the modern localized route with new graphics and BGM; Windows is the highest-fidelity and easiest capture option.
primary.how_to_play: Play Langrisser I through Langrisser I & II on Windows/Steam; use Genesis/Warsong or PC Engine/Saturn versions only for historical comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: The remake changes visuals/music and presentation; use older versions only when documenting original-era differences.

entries.title: Langrisser II
entries.definitive_edition: Langrisser I & II remake on Windows

emulation.notes: No emulation needed for the primary route; emulate Mega Drive, Super Famicom, PC-FX, Saturn, or PlayStation only for historical comparison.

primary.why: The modern Langrisser I & II remake gives Langrisser II a localized PC route with new graphics and BGM; it is the highest-fidelity practical version for a full playthrough.
primary.how_to_play: Play Langrisser II through Langrisser I & II on Windows/Steam; preserve Der Langrisser, PC-FX, Saturn, and classic Windows as comparison versions.

entries.remaster_caveats: The modern remake changes presentation; compare Der Langrisser and Dramatic Edition separately if documenting historical branch/version differences.

entries.title: Langrisser III

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 for upscaled capture, or Sega Saturn/Windows only for version comparison.

primary.why: Langrisser III has Saturn, Windows, and later PS2 routes; the PS2 port is the later console release and the cleanest native capture target among documented versions.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation 2 version on hardware or PCSX2 with conservative upscaling; use Saturn/Windows only for historical comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Japan-only; no official English release documented.

entries.title: Langrisser IV

emulation.notes: Use PS1 emulation for clean capture; verify language/translation needs separately.

primary.why: Langrisser IV launched on Saturn and later came to PlayStation and PlayStation Network; the PlayStation route is the later broadly emulatable version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation version on PS1 hardware, PSN-compatible hardware where available, or a PS1 emulator; use the Saturn original for historical comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Japan-only; no official English release documented.

entries.title: Langrisser V: The End of Legend

emulation.notes: Use PS1 emulation for clean capture; verify language/translation needs separately.

primary.why: Langrisser V launched on Saturn, then came to PlayStation and PlayStation Network; the PlayStation route is the later broadly emulatable version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation version on PS1 hardware, PSN-compatible hardware where available, or a PS1 emulator; use the Saturn original for historical comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Japan-only; no official English release documented.

entries.title: Langrisser Millennium

emulation.notes: Try a period-correct Windows setup first; use Flycast for the Dreamcast original if the PC port is impractical.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows 98 PC output, or Dreamcast output via emulator.

primary.why: The Dreamcast spin-off was later ported to Windows 98; the PC route is the most capture-friendly documented version if a legitimate copy can be run.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Windows 98 port on a dedicated retro Windows setup or VM if available; otherwise play the Dreamcast original through hardware capture or Flycast.

entries.remaster_caveats: Spin-off with real-time battles rather than the classic turn-based Langrisser formula.

entries.title: Langrisser Millennium WS: The Last Century

emulation.notes: Use WonderSwan emulation or hardware capture with clean scaling.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: WonderSwan handheld output with emulator scaling.

primary.why: The Last Century is documented as a Japan-only WonderSwan release with no higher-fidelity official port.
primary.how_to_play: Play on WonderSwan hardware with capture or an accurate WonderSwan emulator; prepare language/context notes separately.

entries.remaster_caveats: Japan-only handheld side story; no official remaster documented.

emulation.notes: No emulator solves an online-service dependency; verify archival legality before any footage.

primary.why: Tri-Swords is listed as a 2012 Windows entry in the Langrisser series; no current official play route was found in the public sources consulted.
primary.how_to_play: Treat as a historical online-service entry unless a legitimate playable client/server archive is documented; do not plan a normal live playthrough.

emulation.notes: Hardware capture is the cleanest official route; emulator upscaling can improve capture if legal files are available.

primary.why: Re:Incarnation Tensei is a Nintendo 3DS-only revival with official Western localization; no higher-fidelity port is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo 3DS hardware with capture, or use a 3DS emulator only if you own the game and can dump it legally.

entries.title: Langrisser Mobile
entries.definitive_edition: Current Windows client, if service is available

emulation.emulator: Native Windows or official mobile clients
emulation.notes: Use official clients only; avoid unofficial automation or clients that violate service rules.

primary.why: Langrisser Mobile is documented for iOS, Android, and Windows; Windows is the best capture route for a live-service playthrough when the service is available.
primary.how_to_play: Use the official current Windows client if available in the target region, or the official mobile app for account setup; do not rely on unofficial automation or rule-breaking clients.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live-service content and availability can change; verify current region/server status before planning coverage.
